extracted.intended_audience: students (high-school and college) seeking essay examples and basic writing guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing typical academic essays: deciding length, organizing into introduction/body/conclusion, creating clear central ideas and paragraph topic sentences, using other essays for brainstorming, and citing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay length adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, the length requirements are indicated in your assignment sheet. It can be words, paragraphs, or pages given as a range (300–500 words) or a particular number (5 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure about length, clarify with your tutor; when in doubt follow the assignment sheet. The site also offers a detailed guide on how to write an essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear central idea
rubrics_metrics.description: An essay should have a single clear central idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the entire essay focused on this main idea so that the reader can easily identify the purpose and argument of the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph-level clarity (topic sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paragraph should have a clear main point or topic sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure paragraphs are coherent units that support the central idea; begin paragraphs with a topic sentence and develop that point within the paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: An essay or paper should be organized logically, flow smoothly, and 'stick' together. In other words, everything in the writing should make sense to a reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use logical sequencing, transitions, and consistent argumentation so the essay feels unified and easy to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic essay structure (intro, body, conclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: A basic essay consists of three main parts: introduction, body, and conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following this format will help you write and organize an essay, but remain flexible — let the topic and specific assignment guide the writing and organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use essays for brainstorming (but transform and cite)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the essays you found on a topic and extract the ideas from them. Use those ideas for the basis of your own essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not copy; adapt and synthesize ideas. Remember to cite any essays you used for your new essay to avoid plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember to cite any essays you used for your new essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribution is required when drawing on other essays or sources; follow the citation style required by your assignment or instructor.
